Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to offer users a way to migrate their data and settings from an existing app to a designated replacement app. Here are the details.

iOS will make switching apps easier

While it's not a common occurrence, developers sometimes retire an existing app and replace it with a new one, requiring users to switch to a separate standalone app.

Even though most developers work hard to make the transition as smooth as possible, migration can still require some effort from users, especially when data isn't stored in the cloud.

With iOS 27.2, Apple will address this issue through a system-managed migration process that can transfer an app's data and supported settings to its designated replacement app before the old app is deleted.

Based on code present in iOS 27.2 beta 1, users will see the following prompt:

"The developer of your existing '%1$@' app recommends transferring your data and settings to a new app called '%2$@'. Your iPhone can do this for you now, before you get started with the new app. Afterwards, the old app will be deleted from this iPhone."

Users will then have the option to choose "Transfer App Data & Settings" or "Don't Transfer Anything." If a user declines the migration, iOS will show a second confirmation warning noting that some preferences (including notification and location settings) may need to be reconfigured.

To clarify, this feature appears to be limited to cases where a developer replaces their own app with a designated replacement app, rather than for migrating data between apps from different developers.

Based on the current implementation, iOS can migrate a number of system-level settings and permissions, including:

  • Privacy, Location, and Health authorization decisions
  • Notification settings, including accessory notification settings
  • Per-app Do Not Disturb and Focus Mode settings
  • App Lock and protection settings
  • CarPlay icon arrangement order and compatible widget layouts
  • Live Activities and accessory Live Activities
  • Access permissions to related accessories
  • LaunchServices preferences, fonts, capture-related defaults, call data, and Secure Element services

We'll continue to monitor changes to this framework throughout the iOS 27.2 beta testing cycle, and will report back once we learn more about how developers are implementing this feature.
